categories.main_business_segments: Doosan Fuel Cell Co., Ltd. primarily operates in the power generation fuel cell sector, focusing on supplying fuel cell equipment for power plants and providing long-term maintenance services. The company also pursues new business areas including ship fuel cells and mobility power packs for commercial vehicles, leveraging its core fuel cell technologies.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company specializes in Phosphoric Acid Fuel Cell (PAFC) technology for power generation, with ongoing development in Solid Oxide Fuel Cell (SOFC) technology for both power generation and ship applications. Production involves manufacturing key components such as MBOP (Mechanical Balance of Plant), EBOP (Electrical Balance of Plant), and cell stacks, with efforts on localization and long-term supply contracts to ensure stable procurement.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers include public and private power generation operators and special purpose companies (SPCs) in South Korea. The company also targets emerging markets in China and Australia, focusing on hydrogen energy projects and clean hydrogen power generation. New markets include shipbuilding and commercial vehicle sectors for fuel cell applications.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company’s main operations and production facilities are located in Iksan, Jeollabuk-do, South Korea. It actively pursues overseas business opportunities, particularly in China and Australia, through partnerships and export contracts. The domestic market remains the largest and most developed for its fuel cell products.
categories.supply_chain_position: Doosan Fuel Cell operates primarily in the midstream and downstream segments of the hydrogen and fuel cell supply chain, manufacturing fuel cell systems and supplying them to power plant operators, along with providing long-term maintenance services. It sources key raw materials and components but focuses on system integration and service delivery.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company emphasizes R&D to enhance product competitiveness and develop new fuel cell technologies, including next-generation PAFC and SOFC systems. Strategic initiatives include commercialization of the Tri-gen model producing electricity, heat, and hydrogen simultaneously, and expansion into ship fuel cells and mobility power packs. Collaboration with global partners like Ceres Power and HyAxiom supports technology development and market entry.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is generated mainly through sales of fuel cell main equipment (56% of 2023 sales) and long-term maintenance service contracts (44%). Sales are primarily made via competitive bidding processes with public and private power producers. The company also engages in project development and financing for special purpose companies.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Doosan Fuel Cell holds the leading domestic market share in South Korea’s power generation fuel cell market with approximately 51% cumulative installed capacity. It competes with global players such as Bloom Energy and FuelCell Energy. The company leverages its high efficiency, reliability, and diversified fuel compatibility to maintain competitive positioning.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: As of 2023, the company reported revenues of approximately KRW 260.9 billion with an operating profit of KRW 1.6 billion and a net loss of KRW 8.5 billion. Total assets stood at KRW 1.07 trillion with liabilities of KRW 558 billion, reflecting a debt ratio of 108.9%. The company experienced a revenue decline in 2023 due to delayed project deliveries but is investing heavily in SOFC production capacity and new business areas for future growth.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Doosan Fuel Cell offers high-efficiency, stable, and environmentally friendly fuel cell systems with superior combined heat and power efficiency (~90%). Its products support multiple fuels (natural gas, LPG, hydrogen) and provide long-term durability with 10-year warranties on core components. The Tri-gen model uniquely produces electricity, heat, and hydrogen simultaneously, enabling integrated energy solutions and cost-effective onsite hydrogen supply.
